aetobarbakinoides:research:1.title: 2026 in archosaur paleontology (research: General pseudosuchian research)

facts.statement: Aetobarbakinoides lived during the late Carnian and early Norian stages of the Late Triassic.
facts.quote: Fossils have been found from the Santa Maria Supersequence of the late Carnian and early Norian stages

facts.statement: Aetobarbakinoides is considered one of the oldest known aetosaurs.
facts.quote: making Aetobarbakinoides one of the oldest aetosaurs

facts.statement: The genus is known solely from the holotype specimen CPE2 168.
facts.quote: Aetobarbakinoides is known only from the holotype specimen CPE2 168

facts.statement: Fossils were discovered near São Pedro do Sul in the center of Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil.
facts.quote: It was found near the city of São Pedro do Sul, in the center of Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil

facts.statement: The specimen was collected from the Inhamandá locality within the Hyperodapedon Assemblage Zone.
facts.quote: It was collected in the Inhamandá locality, from the Hyperodapedon Assemblage Zone

facts.statement: The holotype was originally assigned to Stagonolepis robertsoni by Lucas and Heckert in 2001.
facts.quote: CPE2 168 was assigned by Lucas & Heckert (2001) to Stagonolepis robertsoni

facts.statement: Aetobarbakinoides is the first aetosaur diagnosed without osteoderms in its original description.
facts.quote: It is the first aetosaur to be diagnosed in its original description without osteoderms

facts.statement: Aetobarbakinoides is closely related to the genera Aetosauroides and Neoaetosauroides.
facts.quote: Aetobarbakinoides is most closely related to Aetosauroides and Neoaetosauroides

facts.statement: Known fossils include neck and back vertebrae, ribs, and limb bones such as the scapula, humerus, tibia, and foot bones.
facts.quote: Aetobarbakinoides is known from neck and back vertebrae, ribs, and several limb bones including the scapula, humerus, tibia, and foot bones

facts.statement: Most distinguishing features of the genus are found in its vertebrae.
facts.quote: Most of the distinguishing features of Aetobarbakinoides are found in its vertebrae

facts.statement: It is a medium-sized aetosaur estimated to be about 2 meters in total length.
facts.quote: Aetobarbakinoides is a medium-sized aetosaur, it has been estimated to have been about 2 m in total length

facts.statement: The genus was first named by Julia B. Desojo, Martin D. Ezcurra, and Edio E. Kischlat in 2012.
facts.quote: Aetobarbakinoides was first named by Julia B. Desojo, Martin D. Ezcurra and Edio E. Kischlat in 2012

facts.statement: The specific name 'brasiliensis' refers to Brazil, where the holotype was found.
facts.quote: The specific name refers to Brazil, the country in which the holotype was found

facts.statement: The original study suggests Aetosaurinae is paraphyletic, representing an early grade that evolved into Desmatosuchinae and Typothoracisinae later in the Triassic.
facts.quote: This study suggests that Aetosaurinae is paraphyletic, and that aetosaurines represent a grade of early aetosaurs that developed into desmatosuchines and typothoracisines later in the Triassic

facts.statement: Unlike most other aetosaurs, Aetobarbakinoides is diagnosed primarily by vertebral features rather than osteoderms.
facts.quote: most other aetosaurs are diagnosed by features in bony plates called osteoderms, which are by far the most common material

facts.statement: It is debated whether Aetobarbakinoides is more closely related to aetosaurines based on osteoderms or to desmatosuchines based on vertebrae.
facts.quote: Features of its osteoderms suggest a close relationship with aetosaurines, but its vertebrae are more similar to desmatosuchines

facts.statement: The genus Aetobarbakinoides was described by Desojo and colleagues in 2012.
facts.quote: Desojo et al. 2012

facts.statement: Aetobarbakinoides belongs to the family Stagonolepididae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Stagonolepididae

facts.statement: Aetobarbakinoides is classified as a reptile.
facts.quote: Class: Reptilia

facts.statement: The type species of the genus Aetobarbakinoides is Aetobarbakinoides brasiliensis.
facts.quote: Type species: Aetobarbakinoides brasiliensis

facts.statement: Aetobarbakinoides lived from the Carnian to the Norian stages, between 237 and 205.7 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Carnian to Norian (237 to 205.7 million years ago)

facts.statement: Only one fossil occurrence of Aetobarbakinoides has been recorded.
facts.quote: Fossil occurrences recorded: 1

facts.statement: A 2026 study by Ponce, Cerda, and Desojo used histology of limb bones in Aetobarbakinoides brasiliensis to demonstrate diverse growth rates among pseudosuchians.
facts.quote: Evidence from the study of the histology of appendicular elements of Saurosuchus galilei, Sillosuchus longicervix, Aetobarbakinoides brasiliensis, Aetosauroides scagliai, Gracilisuchus stipanicicorum, Tarjadia ruthae and Riojasuchus tenuisceps, indicative of diversity of growth rates of the studied pseudosuchians, is presented by Ponce, Cerda & Desojo (2026).
